items.followUp: What is the function of the caecum?

rubric.why: Identifies the appendix and where it is found.
rubric.description: Defines the appendix as a small, blind-ended tube attached to the caecum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a small blind-ended tube attached to the caecum.

rubric.why: States its significance in human digestion.
rubric.description: Notes that it is vestigial in humans and has no important digestive function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as vestigial or stating that it has no important digestive function.

modelAnswer: The appendix is a small, blind-ended tube attached to the caecum of the large intestine.
It is vestigial in humans and has no important function in digestion.

items.followUp: What is bile, and where is it stored?

rubric.why: Identifies the gall bladder and its location.
rubric.description: Describes the gall bladder as a small sac situated beneath the liver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a sac beneath or attached to the liver.

rubric.why: Gives its main function.
rubric.description: States that it stores bile produced by the liver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it stores bile.

modelAnswer: The gall bladder is a small sac situated beneath the liver.
It stores bile produced by the liver.

items.followUp: Write two functions of the kidneys.

rubric.why: Names a major liver function.
rubric.description: States that the liver produces or secretes bile.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the production or secretion of bile.

rubric.why: Names another valid liver function.
rubric.description: Gives another role, such as detoxifying harmful substances, converting ammonia to urea, or storing glycogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid role other than bile production.

modelAnswer: The liver produces bile, which helps in the digestion of fats.
It detoxifies harmful substances in the blood.

items.followUp: How does humidity affect the rate of transpiration?

rubric.why: States the effect of rising temperature on transpiration.
rubric.description: Explains that an increase in temperature increases the rate of transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that higher temperature increases the rate.

rubric.why: Explains the reason for the change in rate.
rubric.description: Links higher temperature to faster evaporation of water from leaf surfaces and/or faster diffusion of water vapour out of the leaves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation involving faster evaporation or water-vapour loss.

modelAnswer: As temperature rises, the rate of transpiration generally increases.
Higher temperature speeds up evaporation of water from leaf surfaces and the loss of water vapour from leaves.

items.followUp: Explain how transpiration pull helps water move up a plant.

rubric.why: Identifies cohesion between water molecules.
rubric.description: States that water molecules cohere, keeping the water column continuous in the xylem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining cohesion and its role in maintaining a continuous water column.

rubric.why: Explains the tension or pull that moves water upward.
rubric.description: States that transpiration from leaves creates tension that pulls the continuous xylem water column upward from the roots.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking transpiration-induced tension to upward movement of water.

modelAnswer: The cohesion-tension theory explains the upward movement of water through xylem.
Cohesion between water molecules maintains a continuous water column, and transpiration from leaves creates tension that pulls this column upward from the roots.

items.followUp: What is the role of red blood cells?

rubric.why: Identifies platelets as components of blood.
rubric.description: Describes platelets as small cell fragments present in blood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying platelets as blood cell fragments.

rubric.why: States their main function.
rubric.description: Explains that platelets help blood clot and prevent excessive blood loss.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating their role in clotting or preventing blood loss.

modelAnswer: Platelets are small cell fragments present in the blood.
They help blood to clot at a wound and prevent excessive blood loss.

items.followUp: Write a short note on any three careers related to Biology.

rubric.why: Recognises a biology-related medical career and its work.
rubric.description: Medicine: doctors use biological knowledge to diagnose and treat diseases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming medicine or doctors and describing their work.

rubric.why: Recognises the application of biology to crop production.
rubric.description: Agriculture: biological knowledge is used to improve crops and their production.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming agriculture and describing a relevant role.

rubric.why: Recognises a career involving aquatic organisms.
rubric.description: Fisheries: biology is applied to the breeding, rearing, or management of fish and other aquatic organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming fisheries and describing a relevant role.

rubric.why: Recognises a career involving forests and their conservation.
rubric.description: Forestry: biological knowledge is used to manage and conserve forests.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming forestry and describing a relevant role.

rubric.why: Recognises a career involving the care and breeding of animals.
rubric.description: Animal husbandry: biology is used in the breeding, rearing, and care of livestock.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming animal husbandry and describing a relevant role.

modelAnswer: Medicine: Doctors use biology to diagnose and treat diseases in humans.
Agriculture: Biological knowledge helps improve crops and crop production.
Fisheries: Biology is used to breed, rear, and manage fish and other aquatic organisms.
Forestry: Biologists help manage and conserve forests.
Animal husbandry: Biology is applied to the breeding, rearing, and care of livestock.

items.followUp: What is meristematic tissue? Name its three types based on their position in a plant.

rubric.why: Gives the defining feature of meristematic tissue.
rubric.description: States that meristematic tissue consists of actively and continuously dividing cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its actively dividing cells.

rubric.why: Describes the position and role of apical meristems.
rubric.description: Apical meristems occur at the tips of roots and shoots and increase length.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the apical type with its location or role.

rubric.why: Describes the position or role of intercalary meristems.
rubric.description: Intercalary meristems occur at the bases of leaves or internodes and help elongation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the intercalary type with its location or role.

rubric.why: Describes the position or role of lateral meristems.
rubric.description: Lateral meristems occur along the sides of stems and roots and increase their thickness or girth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the lateral type with its location or role.

modelAnswer: Meristematic tissue is made of cells that divide actively and continuously.
Apical meristems occur at the tips of roots and shoots and increase the plant’s length.
Intercalary meristems occur at the bases of leaves or internodes and help these regions elongate.
Lateral meristems occur along the sides of stems and roots and increase their thickness or girth.
